newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday March 28.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Centre-right opposition parties said they would oppose the 15.5 trillion lire 1997 mini-budget approved by the government, while business leaders called for the withdrawal of the package which includes measures forcing companies to pay tax advances on their huge pools of severance payment funds (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi said he would start negotiations over welfare state reforms with "all the country's responsible forces" next month (all).
* The United Nations criticised Italy's handling of the Albanian refugees' crisis, blaming Rome for blocking the sea routes to the southern shores of Italy (all).
* Energy group ENI will cut the price of petrol by 50 lire a litre at its major self service distributors run by its units Agip and IP by March 29 (all).

* CIR, the industrial holding company of Carlo De Benedetti, posted a consolidated net profit of 320 billion lire in 1996 from a 288.3 billion loss in 1995. The company said it had reduced its holding in information technology group Olivetti and now holds a stake of eight percent (all).
* Finmeccanica, the engineering, aerospace and defence arm of state industrial holding IRI posted a consolidated net loss of 540 billion lire in 1996 (all).
* A report by national statistics institute ISTAT showed that employment in Italian industrial firms with more than 500 employees fell 3.4 percent year-on-year in December (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
